title: unified-rollouts: enhanced probing for staged shadow/canary auto-rollback
author: Aisha Khan
description: Context: we observed instability in staged shadow + canary rollouts where probes that exercise model outputs (semantic similarity, reranker score distributions) were noisy at low sample rates which caused spurious auto-rollbacks. Motivation: reduce false positives while preserving fast automatic rollback on real regressions. This PR adds a probing controller that aggregates staggered probes, applies adaptive smoothing and confidence thresholds, and ties probe signals to the unified rollouts engine to make rollback decisions more robust. Design summary: (1) staggered probing schedule for shadow traffic to increase sample diversity without increasing steady-state traffic; (2) adaptive EWMA smoothing on metric time-series with window tuned per-metric; (3) confidence estimator using bootstrap sampling to ensure significance before triggering rollback; (4) probe-driven hysteresis and cooldown windows to avoid flip-flop; (5) optional strict-mode toggle for high-sensitivity enterprise customers. Includes migration: rollout policy schema extended with "probes" stanza (backwards-compatible defaults). Testing: unit tests for scheduler and smoothing functions, integration test that runs end-to-end in perf-canary harness, and e2e in perf-canary with synthetic regressions. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated, enable in canary for internal customers for 72h then unflag. Related work: ENG-2148 (false-positive rollbacks), ENG-2172 (probe-scheduler), related PRs in generated_data include multiple unified-rollouts autorollback improvements. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] perf validation (synthetic) - [x] docs update - [x] feature flag gating
